content: Segmentation in biology refers to the division of certain metazoan bodies and plant body plans into a series of semi-repetitive segments. This concept is closely associated with the broader idea of modularity. Examples of segmented animals include annelids and arthropods, whereas segmentation is absent in cnidarians. In vertebrates, the vertebrae are inherited in a segmented manner, which facilitates the adaptation of these animals to possess the appropriate number of spinal cord segments within the vertebral column. This phenomenon has been extensively studied in mice. Among plants, horsetails serve as a clear example of segmentation. Segmentation enables a high degree of specialization in different regions of the body. While regional specialization is observed to some extent in annelids, it represents a more advanced evolutionary development in the body plan of arthropods. The establishment of such a segmented body pattern is a key topic in the study of morphogenesis.
